京鑼主要由銅合金鑄造而成，通常採用銅與錫的混合比例製作鑼面，以獲得最佳的音色效果: The jing is mainly cast from a copper alloy, usually copper mixed with tin to make the face, which gives the best timbre. The face is cast and hammered with care so that its thickness is even and its tone true. The rim is specially treated to strengthen the structure. A traditional jing usually comes with a wooden beater whose head is covered in cloth or leather, so that the player can adjust the sound of the stroke as needed; the wooden handle is easy to control, and the whole design is both artistic and functional.
京鑼屬體鳴樂器，以包布鼓槌敲擊黃銅鑼面發聲。其音色可因敲擊力度改變：輕擊時聲音較: The jing is an idiophone, sounded by striking its brass face with a cloth-wrapped beater. The timbre changes with the force of the stroke: struck lightly the sound is softer and rings longer, struck hard it is louder and carries a growl. Though a percussion instrument, the jing has a fixed pitch, and a single stroke produces a harmonious sound. By pitch it divides into Amjing, which is lower, and Sujing, which is higher. The source does not mention differences from other instruments of the family, so only its fixed pitch and its two registers, low and high, can be confirmed.
京鑼是韓國傳統音樂中的重要打擊樂器，為一種大型銅鑼。其起源可追溯至東亞古代的金屬: The jing is an important percussion instrument in Korean traditional music, a large bronze gong. Its origin can be traced to the ancient metal-instrument-making tradition of East Asia, and it owes much to the ancient Chinese bronze-gong culture. In Korea it matured during the medieval period and became a core instrument of both court music and folk music.
京鑼的發展與韓國音樂體系密切相關，特別是在三國時期至朝鮮王朝期間。它廣泛應用於農: The development of the jing is closely tied to the Korean musical system, especially from the Three Kingdoms period to the Joseon dynasty. It was widely used in nongak, shaman music, court aak and other traditional forms, where it set the beat and built the atmosphere. The jing is known for a deep, powerful timbre that produces a lasting resonance.
京鑼見於傳統韓國音樂，尤其四物遊戲、農樂、大吹打，用以維持節拍；亦用於農民、巫教: The jing appears in traditional Korean music, especially samul nori, nongak and daechwita, where it keeps the beat; it is also used at rites and special occasions in farmers', shamanic, Buddhist and military music. In samul nori it is one of the four percussion instruments and takes part in building the rhythm.
京鑼（Jing，韓文징）是韓國傳統音樂中的大型鑼，屬體鳴樂器。通常以高品質黃銅製: The jing (Korean 징) is a large gong in Korean traditional music and an idiophone. It is usually made of high-quality brass and struck with a beater padded with cloth at one end, which softens the timbre. It is common at rites and special occasions in farming, shamanic, Buddhist and military music, and it appears in percussion line-ups such as samul nori, pungmul and daechwita, where it is mainly responsible for the beat. By pitch it falls into a low and a high kind; though a percussion instrument, it has a fixed pitch, and it can produce a soft, drawn-out sound or a great roaring one.
站於琴前，雙手持棒敲擊琴鍵中央。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使: Stand at the instrument and strike the centre of the bars with a stick in each hand. Take the instrument itself in your hands and set it vibrating by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking; different parts and different amounts of force give different timbres. Begin by settling into the correct hold on the instrument, and once the basic way of sounding it is secure, work on rhythm patterns and melodies. Strike the surface with a finger or a drumstick and let the rebound lift it naturally, keeping the wrist loose.
隨著韓國文化的傳播，京鑼逐漸為國際所知。在現代，它不僅保存於傳統音樂演奏中，也成: As Korean culture spread, the jing became known internationally. Today it is not only kept alive in traditional performance but is also an important object of cultural-heritage protection, and it shows the distinctive appeal of Korean traditional art on the world-music stage.
